title: Starting — pre-flight checks
blurb: Parallel health checks (database, SAP AI Core, Gmail) run before any fetching, plus a source-simulation precheck. If a required system is unreachable, or a URL source was never simulated, the run aborts here.

title: Collecting — fetch from sources
blurb: Pulls new items from every configured source (RSS, Twitter/X, crawled URL sources, email inbox) and stamps each item's publisher plus a baseline issuing authority (configured, with AI-inferred fallback). Authority is later confirmed/overridden from the matched law in Law Match. Each source is anchored to its own last-fetch date so nothing is re-pulled.

title: Filtering — drop stale by date
blurb: Applies each source's date window (lookback). Date-only — relevance is decided later by the Impact gate, not here.

title: Comparing — exact dedupe
blurb: Cheap exact/near-duplicate detection (source id, URL, hash, entity fingerprint) before the expensive L2 fetch, so duplicates never cost an AI call. Duplicates are kept (stamped rank 0), never dropped.

statuses.label: NEW
statuses.meaning: First time this item has been seen.

statuses.label: DUPLICATE
statuses.meaning: Identical to another item — stamped rank 0, kept, never emailed.

title: L2 Fetch — full-article detail + law refs
blurb: Follows each item's URL, extracts the full article, and makes one AI call for a factual English summary plus the law/act references. Runs FIRST among the semantic stages so everything downstream (Glossary, Law Match, Impact, Rank) works on the full article, not the headline. Grounded with the profile's registered laws. Mandatory: if any fetch fails, the run stops.

title: Glossary Match — topic labels
blurb: Matches the full-article summary against the profile glossary (deterministic, no AI) and assigns canonical topic labels. Rank-significant items that match nothing are later flagged as glossary gaps.

title: Law Match — resolve the cited law
blurb: Resolves the cited law to the profile's Law Reference registry (number-first, then name), giving each item a language-independent law_id — the primary cross-language grouping identity. Also resolves the issuing authority from the matched law. A cited law that isn't registered is flagged as 'suggested'.

title: Reconcile — cross-language dedupe & change
blurb: Now that the law identity is known, reconciles items that Comparing left as NEW: a match against a prior run or an earlier item this run (even in another language) becomes UPDATE or DUPLICATE, and recurrence is tracked.

statuses.label: UPDATE
statuses.meaning: Same law as a prior item, kept visible as a developing change.

statuses.label: REPEATED
statuses.meaning: The same law/story has recurred across 3 or more runs.

statuses.label: DUPLICATE
statuses.meaning: Same law as an earlier item this run (e.g. another language).

title: RCM Match — proposed title
blurb: Generates an English, RCM-styled title per item and matches it against the cached RCM reference titles: 'tracked' if it maps to an existing RCM regulation, else 'net-new'. The proposed title becomes the item's headline in Review and speeds announcement grouping.

title: Impact — relevance & change assessment
blurb: One AI call over the summary, grounded by the profile's editable relevance rubric. Emits operational_impact (0–3), whether an actual regulatory change is confirmed, whether preparation is required, and the effective date. This is where relevance is decided — Rank then only scores significance.

title: Timing — when it takes effect
blurb: Deterministic (no AI): classifies the effective date + law status into a timing signal — immediate, upcoming/future, or none/past — which feeds the Rank gate.

title: Rank — significance 1–5 (deterministic)
blurb: A deterministic signal-fusion gate scores significance 1–5 from the upstream signals (glossary, law, RCM, authority, operational impact, timing, change flags) — no AI call. Relevance is already handled by Impact. Email is sent only for rank ≥ threshold (default 3).

ranks.label: Urgent
ranks.meaning: Confirmed change, high operational impact, immediate effect

ranks.label: Signal
ranks.meaning: On-topic (glossary/law match) but no operational impact

ranks.label: Noise
ranks.meaning: No operational impact and no glossary/law match

title: Sending — email digest
blurb: Items at or above the rank threshold (default 3) are composed into an AI-grouped HTML digest and sent via Gmail on a separate thread. Skipped in test mode; resendable on failure.

title: Done — run complete
blurb: Results are saved and visible in Review immediately. The email send runs afterward on its own thread; human review is asynchronous and never blocks the run.
